why: replace the scaffold placeholders of the ModCheck overview and its domains and standards indexes with what the tool is and what its documents hold

ops.body: ModCheck is a .NET 8 console tool that loads one mod DLL against the real game assemblies and checks, without launching the game, for the two ways a mod breaks after a game update: a type whose vtable cannot be set up, and a call to a member the game no longer has. It lists every failing type and method and returns exit code 0 (passed), 1 (failures) or 2 (usage). `tools/TestRunner/Invoke-OniTests.ps1` runs it on each test DLL before a game session, and the mod author runs it by hand after a game update: `dotnet run --project common/tools/ModCheck -- <game Managed dir> <mod dll>`.

Files:

- `Program.cs`: the whole tool. `Main` (arguments, assembly resolution, the type and method loops, the exit code), `Report`, `AllMethods` and `Unwrap`.
- `ModCheck.csproj`: console exe on net8.0 with C# 9 and no package references; it does not import `oni-mod.props`.
- `.gitattributes`: line-ending and merge rules for this node's `.context/` files.
- `bin/`, `obj/`: build output, ignored by `common/.gitignore`.

The `.context/` documents of this node: [domains](domains/README.md) (entities, glossary), [standards](standards/README.md) (code style, error handling, naming conventions), `decisions/` and `retrospectives/`.

Documents in this folder:

- [entities](entities.md): `Program` and its helpers, the type-load and JIT checks, inputs and output, the rules ModCheck enforces, key code paths and its caller in TestRunner.
- [glossary](glossary.md): ONI, JIT, CLR, ECall and DIM, and the terms VTable setup failure, missing member, managed directory and warning.

Documents in this folder:

- [code-style](code-style.md): Formatting, C# 9 on .NET 8 with no packages, imports, the one-file structure and comments.
- [error-handling](error-handling.md): Exit codes 0, 1 and 2, the OK, FAIL and WARN output lines, per-type isolation, loader exceptions, host artifacts, unwrapping and assembly resolution.
- [naming-conventions](naming-conventions.md): Project and file names, C# member casing, the two positional arguments and the output vocabulary.
